method: All 11 original studio images and six actual village frames visually inspected. Scores are subjective pixel judgments; builder metrics did not determine acceptance.

correctionResult.family: closed roof enclosure and soffit representation
correctionResult.delta: Enclosure 0.80 to 0.91 (+0.11); trim contacts 0.85 to 0.90; swept profile retained at 0.90. No critical regression.
correctionResult.pixelFinding: Open background strips have become a continuous shaded underside along the far gable overhang. Front-left, rear-right and clay-rear now show a closed roof with coherent gable contact. Porch also reads as a thin solid canopy. Body, doors, loft window, chimney and terrace retain their accepted proportions.
correctionResult.remainingConstructionNotes: The deeper shaded band is a visible overhang underside rather than an open hole. Deliberately plain roof/stone materials are appropriate to the macro gate.

familyLedger.family: closed roof enclosure and soffit representation

assembly.findings: Barrel remains outside the front step and central entry. Rear door sill remains free of terrain intrusion; terrace meets the coastline shelf. The closed roof has not introduced a visible clash with the lower cottage01 annex or cottage03. Local foliage remains clear.
assembly.limitations: Cardinal 90/270 are heavily occluded by frozen neighbors. Front/rear and elevated 45/135 jointly provide the usable contact evidence. Tight cottage01 interface warrants keeping finish/net rack inside the existing plot.

release: Finish may proceed with accepted macro silhouette, root transform, terrace, roof curve and neighboring modules frozen. Finish requires its own attachment and assembly gate.
remainingTargetGap: Net-mender identity details, layered slate, masonry, timber finish and hardware intentionally absent at macro stage. Acceptance is not a claim of exact inferred-reference identity or complete island V2.
